steps.what: Open the changes queued for these applications
Run the test pack against those changes
Read failures before accepting the changes
Sign the test result for these changes
File the signed result on each change

tasks.design: A change already signed for a copy names the application and the expected row. The test job on {DATA_PLATFORM} runs only that pack. The administrator reads the failed rows and signs which changes may go further. A green run is not proof the change is right.
tasks.previous_blocker: Test notes were pasted into mail, so a failure could not be tied to one change id.
tasks.enabler_now: The change form can carry an expected row, and the test job can return pass or fail per change id.
tasks.still_hard: A test that passes on a copy can still be wrong on live data.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator decides which failures matter and signs the result.

ambition.what: Sign a test result the same day the pack finishes

tasks.altitude: Less time copying results, more time on the failures. No change moves because a job went green.

reach.task: Repair only the change ids the administrator marked failed
reach.learn: Which expected rows did not match

evidence.claim: Testing a database change is a pack, a result per change, and a person who decides the failures. A green run is not acceptance.
Digest [S27] says models wrote vulnerable code in a large share of tests, so a clean result is not proof a change is correct.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database, so this test stays on a copy and does not write to production.

assumptions: Focal role is the database administrator. The task ends when the test result is signed. Applying the change is a different task.
Input contract: change id, application name, expected row, copy name. Producer is the signed change. A change with no expected row is not run and stays on a manual list.
Use the platform's own test job before a custom runner.
unknowns: Which applications have a stable copy.
Who signs when the administrator is absent.
research_questions: What share of failures are bad expected rows rather than bad changes?

already_counted.description: The administrator still reads the queue before the pack runs
Judgement of failures stays with the administrator

incremental.description: Update the expected-row template when an application adds a column

approvals.approved_version: test result signed for these change ids

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most changes lack an expected row, so the pack rarely runs. The high case assumes clean packs, but every failure and every pass still takes a human sign-off. No production apply is counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Load the programs and the databases that failed
List the errors against the expected values
Draft modifications from those errors

loop.input: error rows and the modification template
loop.check: Every object name equals the error row
loop.stop: Stop a line when the error has no object name
loop.why_not_simpler: The right correction is not a fixed sentence

steps.what: Sign the modifications that may be applied
Apply the signed modifications on the copy

tasks.design: The same test rows name the programs or databases that failed. A bounded draft in {DOCS} proposes modifications only from those failed fields. The administrator corrects what the draft got wrong and signs one version. Only that version is applied on the copy in {DATA_PLATFORM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fixes were typed straight onto the live object, so there was no version to refuse.
tasks.enabler_now: Failed rows already name the object and the expected value, so a draft can cite them.
tasks.still_hard: The right modification is still a judgement. A later test can still fail.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator corrects the draft and signs the only modification that may be applied.

ambition.what: Sign a correction when the error is understood, not at the next release meeting

tasks.altitude: Less time retyping the error, more time deciding the modification. The apply cannot run unsigned.

reach.task: Stop editing an object the administrator has not signed
reach.learn: Which error ids are still open

evidence.claim: Correcting a database error is a failed row, a proposed modification, and a person who signs it. The next test is a new fact.
Digest [S4] says a coding assistant still needs a person to review the modification it drafts.
Digest [S27] says models wrote vulnerable code in a large share of tests, so the signed modification is not treated as safe because a draft looked clean.
Digest [S28] keeps an unattended write to a production database out of scope. This apply stays on the copy named in the signed version.

assumptions: Focal role is the database administrator. Directing another person to code the same change is still this task when the administrator signs it.
Input contract: error id, object name, failed value, expected value, copy name. Producer is the test result. An error with no object name is corrected by hand and marked manual.
Use the platform's native script job before custom code.
unknowns: Which errors are data, and which are a wrong expected value.
research_questions: How often does the signed modification fail the next test?

already_counted.description: The administrator still checks the failed objects
Editing the draft stays with the administrator

incremental.description: Revise the modification template when a new error class appears

approvals.approved_version: modifications signed for these error ids

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the failed rows lack object names, so the draft is useless. The high case assumes clean rows, but every modification is still signed and the later test is not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train users and answer their questions

steps.what: Build the pack from the signed change

loop.input: signed change fields and the pack template
loop.output: a short pack citing that version
loop.check: Every object name equals the signed change
loop.stop: Stop if the version id is missing
loop.why_not_simpler: How to explain a change to this role is not a stored sentence

steps.what: Sign the pack before the session
Train the users and take their questions
Sign the open questions from the session
File the signed question list

tasks.design: The administrator names a signed change and a role. A pack in {DOCS} is built only from that version. The session stays in the room. Open questions are written down and signed. The {LMS} is not used here because this firm records attendance on the {WORKFLOW} form.
tasks.previous_blocker: Packs were copied from old mail, so a session could teach a change that was never signed.
tasks.enabler_now: The signed change can supply the object names and the reason, which is enough for a short pack.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a user understood the change is only visible in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator runs the session and decides which questions stay open.
tasks.altitude: The room does not shrink. The pack stops being retyped, and the open questions have an owner.

reach.task: Bring a question about a named object
reach.learn: Which change version the session covers

evidence.claim: Training database users is a room session. A pack can be assembled from a signed change. The questions are not a ticket queue.
Digest [S3] says a prompt can fill document fields and can be wrong. The pack is checked against the signed change before the session.

assumptions: Focal role is the database administrator. Users' time in the room is not this role's saving.
Input contract: change version, role name, object names, reason. Producer is the signed change. If the version is missing, the administrator teaches from notes and marks the pack manual.
No model scores who understood the session.
unknowns: Which roles must attend before a change goes live.
research_questions: How many questions are about a different change than the one on the pack?

already_counted.description: The administrator still edits the pack
The session stays in the room

incremental.description: Update the pack template when the change form adds a field

approvals.approved_version: training pack signed for this change version
open questions signed after this session

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes there is no signed version, so the pack is written by hand and the session is unchanged. The high case saves only the pack assembly. The room and the answers are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the support request from junior staff
Match the object on the catalog
Draft the reply from the catalog row

loop.input: catalog row and the reply template
loop.output: a reply that cites the object and the owner
loop.check: The object name equals the catalog row
loop.stop: Stop when the catalog has no such object
loop.why_not_simpler: The cause of an unknown fault is not a stored sentence

steps.what: Sign the support reply for this request
Send the signed support reply

tasks.design: A request on {HELPDESK} names the object, the symptom, and who asked. A reply draft in {DOCS} may cite only the catalog row. The administrator signs it. Junior staff and clients still get a person when the catalog does not explain the fault.
tasks.previous_blocker: Support lived in chat, so a reply could not show which catalog row it used.
tasks.enabler_now: The catalog can return object name, owner, and last signed change, which is enough to start a reply.
tasks.still_hard: A fault the catalog does not explain still needs the administrator.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator decides the reply and refuses one that cites no object.

ambition.what: Answer a catalog-shaped request the same day, and keep the odd faults

tasks.altitude: Repeated catalog questions take less rewriting. The hard faults stay with the administrator.

reach.task: Attach the object name before asking

evidence.claim: Technical support for a database is a request, a catalog lookup, and a person who signs the reply. Junior staff still need the conversation when the catalog is silent.
Digest [S1] says a service desk can suggest a category and draft a knowledge line for a person to review. That fits a support reply, not a schema change.

assumptions: Focal role is the database administrator. Time spent by junior staff and clients is not saved here.
Input contract: requester, object name, symptom, catalog owner. Producer is the person asking. A request with no object name stays in the queue for a conversation.
Use the help desk's own reply form before custom code. No score of the person who asked.
unknowns: Which symptoms already have a signed reply.
research_questions: What share of requests have no object name?

already_counted.description: The administrator still edits the reply
Unknown faults stay a human decision

incremental.description: Retire a reply template when the catalog owner field changes

approvals.approved_version: support reply signed for this request

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most requests are free text with no object, so the draft does not fire. The high case assumes clean requests, but every reply is still signed and the conversation about an unknown fault is not saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The administrator stops retyping test notes and support replies, and spends the week on failed changes, real errors, and the questions only a person can answer.
reach: Junior staff receive the signed reply instead of a half-written chat.
Users leave a training session with the questions that were still open.
skills_to_grow: Treat a passing test as a fact about the copy, not as permission to change production.
Correct an error only from the failed row, then sign the modification.
Keep training and support as conversations, with the pack and the reply on a signed version.
role.ambitious_version: Every tested change has a signed result, and every support reply names the catalog object it is about.
